name: Limited Use Motorcycle
description: A moped: a motor vehicle with two or three wheels and a seat or saddle whose maximum performance speed is 40 mph or less, in class A (over 30 to 40 mph), class B (over 20 to 30 mph) or class C (20 mph or less). An electric moped qualifies by its top speed, and an e-bike past the bicycle with electric assist limits lands here when it has a seat and tops out at 40 mph. Defined by Vehicle and Traffic Law §§121-b and 121-c.
restrictions: Two or three wheels and a seat or saddle for the operator, with a maximum performance speed of 40 mph or less
Class A tops out over 30 mph up to 40 mph, class B over 20 mph up to 30 mph, and class C at 20 mph or less
Only a model its manufacturer has certified as a limited use motorcycle can be registered
Registered with the DMV, every class; no title required
Since January 7, 2025, a New York dealer must register a moped at the time of sale
Class A riders need a motorcycle license (class M or MJ); class B and class C riders need a driver's license of any class
Liability insurance required for class A and class B, and for a class C used as a rental
Class A and class B riders must wear a helmet
Class A may use any traffic lane; class B and class C stay in the right-hand lane or on the shoulder except to turn left
Class A needs a safety inspection
